have deliberated over leaving an honest review for this GP practice for many years, but, after years of declining levels of service, I feel obliged. As others have said, there is no longer an alternative to booking an appointment other than filling in an e-Consult form online. This has been adopted by the GP practice since the ‘pandemic’, and replaces years of not being able to make an appointment, but being forced to treat the GP office like a walk-in clinic to arrive in either an unwell state to sit in a busy waiting room for up to 2-3 hours or with a non-urgent health issue that you just wish to discuss with your GP, and would have been better at an agreed appointment time.

I have asked repeatedly if this will ever change, and was told by reception this morning that if I have an issue with the e-Consult service that I should take it up with the external provider. It used to take a few minutes to call reception to request a call from a GP or to book an appointment with a nurse practitioner. It now takes between 30-45 minutes to complete an online form that is not fit for purpose, and is often rejected. The result is that either (1) you need to call the practice (to suffer through the long winded recorded message) to be told to complete the ‘Admin form’ or (2) you have to wait for up to 7 days for a 2-line email reply with a dismissive words from a GP. The most common advice? Fill in an e-Consult form…

I no longer contact Leven unless instructed to do so (e.g., for a cervical smear) - which appears to be their goal to not see patients? Why is it that other Edinburgh GP practices can still function with a full service where patients can call to book an appointment for later the same day or for non-urgent matters in the next few weeks? If you have a choice, do not register at this clinic. Consider going have deliberated over leaving an honest review for this GP practice for many years, but, after years of declining levels of service, I feel obliged. As others have said, there is no longer an alternative to booking an appointment other than filling in an e-Consult form online. This has been adopted by the GP practice since the ‘pandemic’, and replaces years of not being able to make an appointment, but being forced to treat the GP office like a walk-in clinic to arrive in either an unwell state to sit in a busy waiting room for up to 2-3 hours or with a non-urgent health issue that you just wish to discuss with your GP, and would have been better at an agreed appointment time.

I have asked repeatedly if this will ever change, and was told by reception this morning that if I have an issue with the e-Consult service that I should take it up with the external provider. It used to take a few minutes to call reception to request a call from a GP or to book an appointment with a nurse practitioner. It now takes between 30-45 minutes to complete an online form that is not fit for purpose, and is often rejected. The result is that either (1) you need to call the practice (to suffer through the long winded recorded message) to be told to complete the ‘Admin form’ or (2) you have to wait for up to 7 days for a 2-line email reply with a dismissive words from a GP. The most common advice? Fill in an e-Consult form…

I no longer contact Leven unless instructed to do so (e.g., for a cervical smear) - which appears to be their goal to not see patients?
